candidates.title: My Allowance
candidates.description:
Objects hold memories. We save them to remember. But why can't I let go of my giant Beanie Baby collection?!
Philadelphia performance artist Thomas Choinacky humorously assembles ordinary objects and their curious histories. Sitting around a tabletop, a small audience of ten gets an up-close view of the action.
Handheld ephemera from the 1990s come alive: a Beanie Baby collection, VHS of Olympic ice skating routines, Lauryn Hill’s ‘Miseducation’ on a mix tape. These personal artifacts (bought with pocket money) hold peculiar memories and bring up particular questions. What objects and stories…

candidates.title: A Map of Traces
candidates.description: Composed of a series of movement vignettes, "A Map of Traces" evolves through visions of sharp juxtaposition, quiet storytellings, and repetitious chantings that build, break, and birth the next breath. This work draws inspiration from fractured memory, and aims to make a mess, confronting isolation as a trauma response.

candidates.title: Echoes of Dammām
candidates.description:
Echoes of Dammām is a multimedia storytelling performance that follows fragmented stories gathered around dammām, a ritual drumming practice from Bushehr, a port city in southern Iran.
On stage, live narration moves alongside projected video, field recordings, and layered sound. Drums, voices, images, silence, and memory appear in fragments, tracing how grief, resistance, and the struggle for freedom can live inside sonic and bodily practices. Drawing from ethnographic fieldwork in Bushehr, the performance does not tell a single linear story. Instead, it creates an intimate audiovisual space w…

candidates.title: Señor Babyhead
candidates.venue: Asian Arts Initiative Black Box Theater
candidates.description: In an evening of drag, clown, and desperation, Señor Babyhead presents his Día de Muertos Especial. It’s a journey across the Sonoran Desert in which Babyhead encounters artifacts, mirages, and spirits. Who is Señor Babyhead? Only Mexico’s most (washed up) famous sitcom star, desperate to stay relevant and avoid becoming an artifact, himself. It’s an hour of crooning, crawling, and implicating the audience in a dangerous game, or as Theater Beyond Broadway put it, “An act of defiance disguised as cabaret.”

candidates.title: The Mixtape / Andy the Acolyte
candidates.description:
The Mixtape / Andy the Acolyte is a double-bill of original, interactive, fully-improvised solo shows!
The Mixtape sees Alex helping the audience confess their feelings through improvised songs. Through audience suggestions, they help create an improvised mixtape to hopefully inspire those to go for what or who they want the most. (30 minutes)
Andy the Acolyte is your friendly neighborhood devout cultist of an ancient lovecraftian god: the audience! The show follows Andy on a regular workday, but at any moment, any member of the audience can shout out "Hey Andy!" and command him to do ANYTHING…

candidates.title: We Can Always Tell
candidates.description:
We Can Always Tell is a one human production imagined and performed by Kendall Niblett. Using dance, poetry, and visual art as mediums and their body as the instrument, Kendall transposes their experience medically transitioning into an evening length dance performance that emphasizes how all humans know the feeling of their own bodies hurting them, physical limitations, or feeling disturbed by their reflection.
Each facet of Kendall's performance whether it be poetry, movement, or set design is derived from materials collected from their family members, friends, lovers, and passing strangers.…

candidates.title: The Black Pearl and the Frivolous Prince
candidates.description: Paris, 1930s. Al Brown — Latin America’s first world boxing champion — loses his title when his manager drugs him before a fight and he passes out dizzy in the ring. In a grand pivot, Al becomes a cabaret star. A talented singer and dancer, he teaches himself how to play the saxophone. He’s a hit. Then he meets Jean Cocteau – a watershed moment. What happens when a celebrated Panamanian boxer meets a legendary French artist?

candidates.title: Tuzluk
candidates.venue: Asian Arts Initiative Black Box Theater
candidates.description:
Turkish-Colombian-American performer, Izzy Sazak, takes the audience on a wild ride; unpacking the awkward beauty of growing up mixed, caught between two empires worth of daddy issues and messy history. Tuzluk lovingly deconstructs the myth of the neo-liberal hero-man; mixing geopolitics with a hilarious, heartfelt and fast paced examination of identity and inheritance. Tuzluk deftly weaves together a collage of memory and fantasy to tell a story of making peace with the one thing none of us get to choose- one’s fortune.

candidates.title: Bodhi’s Guide to History
candidates.description:
Celebrate America’s 250th Anniversary with Bodhi’s Guide to History, a new play. In this original work, Bodhi leads a walking tour of Center City and gives his unique – and wildly inaccurate – take on American history. Bodhi is proud to do his own research, but tends to veer hilariously off track; but don't worry, the audience will wind up where the play/tour started.
Bodhi’s Guide to History is the creation of playwright Jim Hawkins, who studied theatre at Villanova University.

candidates.title: Cicada Stories
candidates.description: When considering this work, I was drawn to the idea of an anti-performance, creating something that would be unknown to all until it was physically uttered. This work continues my research and examination of a performer’s relationship to viewership and audience. With risk and remix at the forefront, Cicada Stories explores chance, choice, and neutrality in a performance setting. How do our expectations differ as we take on the roles of performer or audience member? How do we impact the performance space just by being? What if our actions taken weeks ago were impacting the now, played out on st…

candidates.title: Baggage From BaghDAD: Becoming My Father’s Daughter
candidates.description:
Baggage From BaghDAD: Becoming My Father’s Daughter is written and performed by award-winning actress Valerie David.
Baggage From BaghDAD: Becoming My Father’s Daughter is a gripping, award-winning solo show that mirrors today's growing intolerance of race and religion. Due to religious persecution during the 1941 “Farhud pogrom,” writer and performer Valerie David’s paternal Middle Eastern Jewish family was forced to flee Iraq and build a new home in America.
This play highlights her family’s struggle to immigrate to a new land and transcend their harrowing past, so that love and the importan…

candidates.title: Liberty City Arts Presents: ‘Beyond’
candidates.description:
Humanity has abandoned a dying Earth. The colony ships are nearing their destination. Two androids are waiting to be dismantled.
Set outside a ship dismantling center in the distant future, Beyond follows androids 142-6 and 513-2 as they face an uncertain fate in a world that no longer needs them. With a libretto by Caitlin Vincent and music by Lisa Neher, this intimate chamber opera stars soprano Olivia Broderick and mezzo-soprano Isabelle Zeledón, with Ting Ting Wong, piano. The evening also features the Philadelphia premieres of Patricia Wallinga's When I Heard the Learn'd Astronomer and Me…

candidates.title: Americana Cosplay
candidates.description:
In a private club, members celebrate the nation's birthday by cosplaying their favorite Americana icons. But the real American myth isn't your Founding Father Fetish. It's the Cowboy. The Capitalist. The Confederate.
Choose your fantasy.
Americana Cosplay is a rowdy, immersive performance that explores how America reinvented itself after the Civil War, and how those inventions became the stories we still tell ourselves today. Exploring the years 1870 through 1890, this darkly funny new work traces the birth of many of the symbols we now mistake for timeless traditions: the lone gunslinger, the…

candidates.title: Elements
candidates.description:
Elements is a month-long immersive exhibition exploring the connection between the human body and the four classical elements: Earth, Water, Fire, and Air. The gallery transforms into a series of evolving environments inspired by a different element each week. Through projection art, soundscapes, and live performances, visitors are invited to slow down, reconnect, and experience the unique energy of each element through art, movement, sound, and community.

candidates.description:
Leslie Elkins and Foursome Performance return to the Fringe Festival and make their Cannonball debut with A Dream Within A Dream, where dance-theater improvisation meets classical piano performance.
What is? What may be? A dancer and pianist improvise a conversation in real time. Between them, a murder of crows grappling with the improbable extinction of idiots. The performance asks what we risk and what we surrender through music and movement partnerships.
This project is the culmination of my sabbatical from teaching at Rowan University. While on leave I practiced improvisational composition…

She falls in love with a self-ordering food kiosk. She needs your help. No really. Explain it to her like she's GIRL.

Through immersive scenery and an ethereal soundscape, the audience will be transported into a snail’s story; A story of discovering what it means to become home to yourself as you become home to someone else.
Learning to slow down and adapt to the surrounding environment is an integral part to becoming a parent for the first time and Katherine has found solace in exploring that experience through this…

candidates.description: Four young women find friendship and solidarity at a well-paying radium dial factory job in the 1920s. Years later, as they realize that their health has been compromised by the work, they unite and support each other while exposing the truth.

candidates.description:
Elio and Luna are lovers bound by the stars, a sun and moon destined to meet every dusk and every dawn, rise and fall, come together and drift apart, across a lifetime. With each reunion a loss, and with each departure a gain. Trans bodies shift and age, both weathered and bolstered by time, only realized through radical transformation, yet still able see the truths in one another. Elio and Luna will follow each other through the stars, and back again.

Can she break free of her world of toys, or will she forever be stuck as a plaything for others? Inspired by EgoPo's 2013 Fringe hit created by Brenna Geffers, starring Emmeline and Lane Savadove.

candidates.title: Christmas Carol: The Rap Musical
candidates.description: Christmas Carol: The Rap Musical reimagines Dickens' classic in a style reminiscent of Hamilton, bringing the energy and storytelling power of hip hop to one of literature's most enduring tales. By showcasing the distinct sounds and styles of hip hop history alongside the traditions of a Victorian Christmas, the show invites you to keep Christmas in your heart all the year (even in September).

candidates.description: MEAT CUTE is a bloody double-feature of two short plays that explore themes of the body, mind, and heart as meat. One play, MEAT PLAY, by Grace Stewart Gardner, is an exploration of the corruption of the modern American meat industry through the story of one worker, Bailey, who has just been assigned to begin their six months of employment on the Killing Floor. Studies show that the longer one spends working on the Killing Floor, where employees are expected to slaughter over 2,000 animals per day, the likelihood of committing a violent crime increases. candidates.title: Zombied
candidates.description:
What happens when your body falls apart? And when those parts follow you, waiting for–something? Do you listen to their grievances? Or scream until they leave? Do they ever leave? ZOMBIED is a gothic supernatural thriller about the fight to defend one thing we all think we deserve: our own bodies.
Queer and disabled people often find their relationships to their bodies irreparably shaped by the negative perceptions of monsters, and at the same time feel comforted by monstrous characters. ZOMBIED is a meditation on this tension, drawing from many of the class literary and gothic monsters we are…
